<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914115_theRebbe_704" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914115_theRebbe_704__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between the repentance of turning from evil and the repentance of doing good and seeking peace, where the latter draws a higher, unbounded light through service.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the distinction between the repentance of "turn from evil" and the repentance of "do good" and "seek peace" is,</t>
    <t s="2">that the repentance of "turn from evil" is that there should not be sins that separate between you and your God,</t>
    <t s="3">and the repentance of "do good" and "seek peace" is that the service should be to draw down a more elevated light.</t>
    <t s="4">For the drawing down that is drawn from above of its own accord,</t>
    <t s="5">from the aspect that He, blessed be He, is the Essence of Good and it is the nature of the Good to do good,</t>
    <t s="6">is with measure and limitation,</t>
    <t s="7">and through service the drawing down is without limit.</t>
    <t s="8">And as is known</t>
    <t s="9">regarding the matter of "These are the generations of Peretz"</t>
    <t s="10">"generations" is written fully (with a Vav),</t>
    <t s="11">which is above even "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created"</t>
    <t s="12">"generations" is written fully (with a Vav),</t>
    <t s="13">"the world was created in its fullness",</t>
    <t s="14">for "generations" written fully that is said regarding the creation of heaven and earth</t>
    <t s="15">(creation from the side of Above)</t>
    <t s="16">the Creator desired that it be with measure and limitation,</t>
    <t s="17">but not so the "generations of Peretz" written fully, which will be</t>
    <t s="18">(at the coming of Moshiach)</t>
    <t s="19">through our deeds and our service</t>
    <t s="20">it is that which Moshiach</t>
    <t s="21">(from the children of Peretz,</t>
    <t s="22">and is called "the one who breaks through")</t>
    <t s="23">will break through all boundaries.</t>
    <t s="24">And within this itself</t>
    <t s="25">(the drawing down through service),</t>
    <t s="26">the drawing down through engagement in Torah</t>
    <t s="27">("seek peace")</t>
    <t s="28">is more elevated than the drawing down through the fulfillment of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="29">("do good").</t>
    <t s="30">For in addition to that through mitzvos the drawing down is in the aspect of makif (encompassing) and through Torah the drawing down is in pnimiyus (inwardness),</t>
    <t s="31">also the drawing down itself is more elevated.</t>
    <t s="32">For through the fulfillment of mitzvos the light of Sovev (the Encompassing) is drawn,</t>
    <t s="33">and through engagement in Torah the Essence of Ein Sof is drawn, which is above even Sovev.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that even a Jew at the level of "Israel" can have the concept of "stumbling in your iniquity," requiring the repentance of turning from evil, and that the mitzvah of repentance applies even to completely righteous individuals.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on the above, that "Return, O Israel, for you have stumbled in your iniquity" is the repentance of "turn from evil,"</t>
    <t s="2">it is understood</t>
    <t s="3">that this, that even one who is at the level of "Israel" has relevance to the matter of "you have stumbled in your iniquity,"</t>
    <t s="4">the intention in this is not</t>
    <t s="5">(only)</t>
    <t s="6">that there is in him some deficiency</t>
    <t s="7">[which is also in the righteous],</t>
    <t s="8">but rather that even sins that separate are relevant to him</t>
    <t s="9">(except that they are in the finest of the fine),</t>
    <t s="10">and therefore the repentance of "turn from evil" must be present in him.</t>
    <t s="11">And this matter</t>
    <t s="12">[that even in the righteous</t>
    <t s="13">(Israel)</t>
    <t s="14">there is also the repentance of "turn from evil"]</t>
    <t s="15">is also understood from the fact that repentance is a mitzvah</t>
    <t s="16">[and in the language of the Alter Rebbe in Igeres HaTeshuvah</t>
    <t s="17">"the mitzvah of repentance"],</t>
    <t s="18">from which it is understood,</t>
    <t s="19">that the mitzvah of repentance is</t>
    <t s="20">(like all mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="21">for every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="22">even for completely righteous individuals.</t>
    <t s="23">And since the mitzvah of repentance is</t>
    <t s="24">(as the Alter Rebbe wrote in Igeres HaTeshuvah there)</t>
    <t s="25">abandoning the sin</t>
    <t s="26">("turn from evil"),</t>
    <t s="27">it is understood,</t>
    <t s="28">that in addition to that even in completely righteous individuals there must be the repentance of "and the spirit shall return to God Who gave it"</t>
    <t s="29">[and as explained in Likkutei Torah</t>
    <t s="30">(our parshah)</t>
    <t s="31">that the root of the soul is the aspect of Elokim</t>
    <t s="32">("Who gave it"),</t>
    <t s="33">which is the aspect of Tzur</t>
    <t s="34">that is above Havayah,</t>
    <t s="35">a concealment that is not in existence,</t>
    <t s="36">and the drawing down of the soul from this aspect is in the manner of</t>
    <t s="37">("Who")</t>
    <t s="38">gave it,</t>
    <t s="39">for all</t>
    <t s="40">who give, give with a generous eye,</t>
    <t s="41">and the matter of the repentance of "and the spirit shall return to God Who gave it" is the return and elevation of the soul to its root and source,</t>
    <t s="42">for even as the soul is invested in the body</t>
    <t s="43">(for the mitzvah of repentance is,</t>
    <t s="44">like all mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="45">specifically for souls in bodies)</t>
    <t s="46">it should be in a state of complete nullification as it was in its root,</t>
    <t s="47">in the aspect of "Elokim Who gave it"],</t>
    <t s="48">there must also be in them repentance in its simple sense.</t>
    <t s="49">And one must understand,</t>
    <t s="50">but in Atzilus</t>
    <t s="51">(even in particular Atzilus)</t>
    <t s="52">it is written "evil shall not sojourn with You,"</t>
    <t s="53">and since the repentance of the righteous is</t>
    <t s="54">(as above from Likkutei Torah)</t>
    <t s="55">"to God Who gave it,"</t>
    <t s="56">above the aspect of "You created it, You formed it, You breathed it into me"</t>
    <t s="57">(Biya"h)</t>
    <t s="58">and above even the aspect of "You placed within me"</t>
    <t s="59">(Atzilus),</t>
    <t s="60">how is it possible that the matter of the repentance of "turn from evil" should exist in them?</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section considers an explanation that the repentance of turning from evil for the righteous relates to a deficiency in their higher service, but concludes that the service of doing good and seeking peace is an addition in holiness itself, not a matter of evil.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And superficially, it could be explained based on what is said in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="2">that one who, due to the superiority of his soul, belongs to the service of the aspect of Ruach</t>
    <t s="3">("do good")</t>
    <t s="4">and all the more so one who belongs to the service of the aspect of Neshamah</t>
    <t s="5">("seek peace"),</t>
    <t s="6">when he is lacking in this service, it is a blemish.</t>
    <t s="7">And furthermore,</t>
    <t s="8">because he is on an elevated level,</t>
    <t s="9">his blemish</t>
    <t s="10">(even though it is in fineness)</t>
    <t s="11">is greater than the actual sin of a simple person.</t>
    <t s="12">And as the Maggid said, the thoughts of completely righteous individuals blemish more than the severe sins of an ignoramus.</t>
    <t s="13">And like "a stain on a garment of a Torah scholar."</t>
    <t s="14">And based on this, it could seemingly be said,</t>
    <t s="15">that the mitzvah of repentance</t>
    <t s="16">(which is abandoning the sin)</t>
    <t s="17">in completely righteous individuals is repentance for that which there was in them a deficiency in the service of "do good" or at least in the service of "seek peace,"</t>
    <t s="18">that even this repentance is abandoning the sin,</t>
    <t s="19">since the blemish caused by this is even greater than the sin</t>
    <t s="20">(in its simple sense)</t>
    <t s="21">of a simple person.</t>
    <t s="22">However,</t>
    <t s="23">from this very thing that they say there are three matters</t>
    <t s="24">("turn from evil,"</t>
    <t s="25">"do good" and "seek peace"),</t>
    <t s="26">it is proven,</t>
    <t s="27">that the service of "do good" and "seek peace" is an addition and ascent in holiness itself,</t>
    <t s="28">and even when there is a deficiency in this service,</t>
    <t s="29">it is not a matter of evil</t>
    <t s="30">(not even in fineness).</t>
    <t s="31">And based on this, one must understand what is the matter of the mitzvah of repentance</t>
    <t s="32">(abandoning the sin)</t>
    <t s="33">in the righteous,</t>
    <t s="34">about which it says "Return, O Israel, etc., for you have stumbled in your iniquity,"</t>
    <t s="35">that even one who is at the level of "Israel" must have in him also the repentance of "turn from evil."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
